title: Small arguments take Cody's rational on the x87 unit, and the last bit can be high
statement: For normal x with |x| < 2^-28, ERF.PRECISE computes p = RN53(RN64(x*P0)) and y = RN53(RN64(p/Q0)): x87 precision 64, the product stored to binary64, then the quotient stored to binary64. P0 = 0x3ff1df5e70c7956b and Q0 = 0x3fefada15778ece6. These are A(4) and B(4) of Cody's 1969 rational for |x| <= 0.5 (3.20937758913846947e3 and 2.84423683343917062e3), both divided by one real scale s = 2873.12583276792695. The two rounded steps can leave the answer 1 unit above the correctly rounded erf(x), as the rows below show. The same route explains GAUSS's small arguments.
basis: 249,300 of 249,300 recorded ERF.PRECISE rows below 2^-27 match, negative arguments included; per-operation binary64 misses rows in the 2^-40 binade alone (131,201 of 131,255). Across the bank the route gains 134,290 ERF.PRECISE rows and 678 GAUSS rows with no row lost in any function.
inferred: That the constants are Cody's is inferred from their ratio and from both being RN(coefficient/s) for one s; s itself is measured from the two constants and no source explains it. That the legacy ERF(x) shares this body is inferred; only ERF.PRECISE and GAUSS rows were scored.

correct.how: mpmath erf at 800 bits from the binary64 input, correctly rounded.
